transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-10-02
Time: 16:00 - 16:50 PT
Duration: ~50 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Maya Chen (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (CISO, Alta), Ethan Cole (Platform Engineer, Alta), Lydia Park (Compliance Manager, Alta)

[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Jordan from Redwood, AE, and with me is Maya our solutions engineer. How are you all?
[00:08] Priya: Good, thanks. Quick note, we're on a tight timeline for procurement — hoping to finalize vendor shortlist by end of month.
[00:15] Jordan: Understood, we'll focus on the compliance and deployment questions you sent. Maya, want to kick off with SOC2/ISO posture?
[00:21] Maya: Yeah, sure. So briefly, Redwood holds SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001, we can share the report summaries and a redacted evidence index. For hosted customers we provide the Type II report, for Dedicated we can arrange a bridge letter and scope details, and for Private deployments customers run the control evidence in their environment, we provide mappings and guidance.
[00:41] Priya: When you say "evidence index" — will that include encryption key rotation logs or are those excluded? We have to show key management proof for certain datasets.
[00:50] Maya: Good question. The index will list control families and sample artifacts — rotation logs for KMS-backed keys are part of our hosted evidence set where we use Redwood-managed keys. If you require customer-managed keys, that's available for Dedicated and Private; we can document KMS integration points, key rotation APIs, and HSM support.
[01:10] Ethan: For Dedicated, can we bring our AWS KMS and have Redwood use customer CMKs? Latency/throughput implications?
[01:18] Maya: Yes, Customer Managed Keys via AWS KMS is supported for Dedicated and Private. Performance impact is minimal because we cache DEKs and only call KMS for key unwrap operations on rotation; that said for high-throughput workloads we recommend using local crypto modules or HSM-backed gateways to avoid per-request KMS calls. We'll pass an architecture note showing KV cache — sorry kv cash — KV cache semantics.
[01:40] Lydia: On audit logs, we need immutable logs with export to our SIEM and 7 years retention. Do you support log streaming or S3 delivery? Also, are logs redactable for PII?
[01:52] Jordan: We have streaming to customer-owned destinations for Dedicated and Private; Hosted can push to a secure log delivery endpoint or provide periodic exports. Redaction is configurable at ingestion for PII patterns, but for compliance we recommend leaving raw logs and using downstream SIEM to handle masking — we can discuss retention/export formats.
[02:12] Priya: Important for us is proof of read access reviews and RBAC audit trail — we need to show who accessed model inference and who exported embeddings.
[02:20] Maya: Our Console surfaces token-level and route-level access logs, we log API key usage and SSO-based user sessions. For Dedicated we can enable deeper audit hooks and longer retention. Role-based access is configurable via RBAC mappings to SAML groups; logs include user id, action, resource, and timestamp.
[02:40] Ethan: On SSO, can you integrate with our Okta via SAML 2.0? We also want SCIM for provisioning.
[02:45] Jordan: Yes, SAML 2.0 and SCIM are supported. For Hosted we integrate with customer IdP for SSO and group sync. For Private we provide an IdP connector pattern. We have docs on the SAML claims we expect; Maya will drop those links.
[03:00] Priya: Do you support JIT user provisioning or do we have to maintain accounts?
[03:05] Maya: SCIM supports provisioning and deprovisioning; JIT is supported for session creation with SAML assertions.
[03:12] Priya: Good. About data residency — we have EU regulated data. Does Hosted allow region pinning? We might need EU-only hosting.
[03:20] Jordan: Hosted provides region pinning to select cloud regions, and Redwood offers Dedicated capacity in specific regions. For strict residency we recommend Dedicated or Private; we can put a contractual clause around data residency.
[03:34] Lydia: Retention policies — can you auto-delete embeddings or raw request payloads after X days? Our policy is 180 days for non-PHI, 30 days for PHI, and some logs need 7 years.
[03:46] Maya: Retention is configurable: for Hosted we offer configurable retention windows for request logs and embeddings; for Dedicated/Private you control retention. We also offer purge APIs for immediate deletion, and proof of deletion logs for audits.
[04:02] Priya: Encryption in transit and at rest — we need TLS 1.2+ and AES-256 at rest. Also FIPS compatibility for certain customers.
[04:10] Maya: We encrypt in transit with TLS; for at rest we use AES-256. FIPS endpoints are available for Private deployments and can be arranged for Dedicated if required.
[04:20] Ethan: If we pick Dedicated, what's the operational model? Do you manage the nodes? Is there an SRE handover?
[04:28] Jordan: For Dedicated Redwood manages the control plane and the GPU fleet operations under the SLA; customers get a dedicated pool and we handle upgrades, but network connectivity and KMS keys are customer-managed. There's an onboarding runbook and a two-week SRE handover during pilot.
[04:46] Priya: Can you provide the SLA contract language around access to logs and auditability? We need that for procurement.
[04:52] Jordan: Yes, we have SLA attachments for enterprise contracts. I'll include the auditability language and sample security appendix.
[05:00] Lydia: A few nitty details: do you maintain a full change log for model versions and a signed checksum for each model artifact? We require integrity verification records.
[05:10] Maya: We maintain model versioning and rollout traces in the Console, and we can provide cryptographic checksums of artifacts on request; we do not currently sign every artifact with a customer-managed signing key by default but that's on the roadmap for Private deployments.
[05:26] Priya: About pen tests and vulnerability scanning — do you provide periodic third-party pen test reports?
[05:32] Jordan: Yes, we run annual third-party pen tests and publish a summary; for Dedicated customers we can provide redacted reports under NDA.
[05:40] Ethan: For the pilot we want to run a baseline performance test against our end-to-end stack including VPC peering. Will Redwood run a latency benchmark and produce a test plan?
[05:50] Maya: Absolutely, we can run a joint benchmark. For Dedicated we'll set up a staging pool and run the tests. We'll publish latency percentiles, throughput, and token-cost numbers.
[06:05] Priya: On legal, we need to know standard data processing addendum (DPA) clauses, sub-processor list, and how you handle law enforcement requests.
[06:15] Jordan: We have a standard DPA that covers processing, subprocessors, and legal request handling; we notify customers per the DPA and log requests. I'll attach the DPA and subprocessor list.
[06:28] Lydia: Can you confirm whether Hosted uses any third-party telemetry or crash-reporting that could capture payloads? We require no payload leakage to analytics.
[06:36] Maya: We avoid capturing full payloads in third-party telemetry; we redact payloads and only emit anonymized telemetry for runtime health. We'll include specifics in the artifact pack.
[06:50] Priya: A hypothetical: if we need air-gapped for PHI, what does Redwood offer?
[06:56] Maya: For air-gapped workloads we offer an on-prem Private deployment package; control plane can be customer-hosted and we ship the inference runtime. That includes an HSM integration and local KMS. It's a heavier onboarding but doable.
[07:12] Ethan: Networkwise, does Redwood support VPC peering, PrivateLink, or do you recommend VPN?
[07:18] Jordan: We support VPC peering and PrivateLink for dedicated and private. Hosted can accept an AWS PrivateLink endpoint for our API. We'll share recommended network patterns.
[07:30] Priya: Regarding RBAC, can we map groups so that certain teams only see embeddings and not full request payloads?
[07:36] Maya: Yes, RBAC is flexible — you can scope routes and data visibility. We can show the access model and an example role matrix.
[07:46] Lydia: For records we need an exportable compliance report that ties controls to evidence. Is that automated?
[07:54] Maya: We have a controls mapping document that maps Redwood features to common frameworks; the export is semi-automated: we provide the mapping and artifacts, then you assemble the customer evidence package. For Dedicated we can customize exports.
[08:08] Priya: Ok, anything else on risk assessment? We need to know data lifecycle, TTL for caches, and KV cache encryption. You've mentioned KV cache earlier as kv cash, can you clarify that?
[08:18] Maya: Apologies for the slip — KV cache is server-side memory of recent tokens and it's encrypted at rest; we persist very short TTLs for cache by default, and you can disable caching for sensitive routes.
[08:34] Ethan: About embeddings - when we ask for embeddings for search, are those stored by default?
[08:39] Maya: By default Hosted does short-term retention for embeddings to allow dedup and speed up reruns; you can opt out and ask for immediate deletion. Dedicated/Private give you full control.
[08:52] Priya: For audit, we need to be able to demonstrate segregation of duties. Can you outline admin roles vs developer roles?
[08:59] Maya: Admin roles include account owners and billing; developer roles are scoped to app-level API keys and route permissions. You can map SAML groups to those roles and we emit the access logs for reviews.
[09:12] Jordan: Quick check — are there any hard blockers today that would prevent you from proceeding to pilot?
[09:17] Priya: Not yet; main blockers are getting SOC2 summaries, clarity on KMS and log export, and Dedicated pricing.
[09:24] Jordan: Great — we'll follow up with the artifacts and pricing.
[09:28] Lydia: One more procurement nuance: we need a clause around data deletion certification post-contract. Is that supported?
[09:35] Jordan: Yes, we can provide data deletion certificates and a documented purge process for enterprise agreements.
[09:41] Ethan: For the pilot, what's the expected lead time to provision Dedicated capacity?
[09:46] Maya: Typically 2-4 weeks after contract signature, depending on region and capacity availability. We can prioritize EU pools if you need residency.
[09:56] Priya: Ok, let's capture next steps. Jordan, please confirm you'll send SOC2 summary, DPA, SAML claim expectations, Dedicated pricing, and a sample SOW.
[10:08] Jordan: Will do. Maya will attach the technical notes and logs delivery options.
[10:14] Priya: Thanks, we'll aim to get the retention matrix over by 2025-10-09.
[10:18] Jordan: Perfect. Anything else?
[10:20] Lydia: No, that's it from Compliance.
[10:22] Ethan: No, thanks.
[10:24] Jordan: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the doc pack and schedule the pilot planning session.

End of transcript.

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-heard words ("KV cash" for KV cache), some interruptions redacted, speaker turns attributed based on calendar but may have slight label drift.
